_comment: Advisories accepted under docs/dependency-policy.md 'Required verification' item 6:
every entry carries reachability, owner, expiry and a compensating control, and an
EXPIRED entry fails the audit rather than silently continuing to suppress. Accept an
advisory ONLY when there is no fixed upstream release; if a fix exists, take the fix.
Enforced by scripts/python_audit.py, invoked from `make python-audit`.

accepted.reachability: Transitive, via cognee only (diskcache is not a direct dependency). The advisory is arbitrary code execution through DiskCache's default pickle serialization, and it requires WRITE access to the cache directory. Boltrig gives cognee a dedicated named volume at BOLTRIG_COGNEE_ROOT (/var/lib/boltrig/cognee) inside a container whose root filesystem is read_only, and nothing but the kernel process writes there. The cache directory is never shared between tenants and is never attacker-writable over any request path, so an actor able to exploit this already holds code execution inside the container.
accepted.compensating_control: Dedicated per-stack named volume (not a shared or world-writable path); read_only root filesystem with only /tmp writable (x-app-hardening); the knowledge subsystem is default-OFF and only reaches cognee when a manifest explicitly enables it.
accepted.reason: No fixed release exists upstream: pip-audit reports the advisory with an empty fix-versions list. Re-check at expiry and take the fix the moment python-diskcache publishes one.

accepted.reachability: Vendored inside the rclone binary copied from the digest-pinned official image into the backup sidecar. The advisory covers xDS RBAC and HTTP/2 handling in gRPC servers; the backup image runs rclone strictly as a CLIENT in a fixed backup loop, serves no gRPC, publishes no ports, and never loads xDS service-mesh configuration, so no server-side path the advisory covers exists in this deployment.
accepted.compensating_control: paths-scoped acceptance in .trivyignore.yaml (usr/local/bin/rclone only, so the finding still fires anywhere else); trivy's expired_at returns the finding to the release gate past 2026-10-23; this ledger fails `make python-audit` on expiry; the backup service is profile-gated, publishes no ports, and mounts the rclone config read-only.
accepted.reason: No fixed release exists upstream: fixed in grpc 1.82.1, but rclone v1.74.4 IS the latest upstream release and carries 1.80.0, so there is nothing to upgrade to. Drop this the moment rclone ships a build with grpc >= 1.82.1 (2026-VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001, D2 - completing the record the .trivyignore.yaml statement already claimed).

accepted.reachability: Vendored inside the rclone binary copied from the digest-pinned official image into the backup sidecar. The advisory is a norm.Iter infinite loop on input containing invalid UTF-8. The backup image runs rclone strictly as a CLIENT in a fixed backup loop against operator-configured remotes; it serves nothing and publishes no ports, but it DOES process names and listings returned by the remote, so reaching the defect requires a compromised operator-provisioned remote - at which point the attacker already holds the off-box backup channel (2026-VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001, F5 as qualified).
accepted.compensating_control: paths-scoped acceptance in .trivyignore.yaml (usr/local/bin/rclone only, so the finding still fires anywhere else); trivy's expired_at returns the finding to the release gate past 2026-10-23; this ledger fails `make python-audit` on expiry; the backup service is profile-gated, publishes no ports, and mounts the rclone config read-only.
accepted.reason: No fixed release exists upstream: fixed in x/text 0.39.0, but rclone v1.74.4 IS the latest upstream release and pins 0.38.0 (master has 0.40.0, unreleased), so there is nothing to upgrade to. Drop this the moment a released rclone carries golang.org/x/text >= 0.39.0 (2026-VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001).

accepted.reachability: NOT UNREACHABLE, and stated so deliberately. chromium runs in both production fleet workers and the browser-cli adapter is ACTIVATED on the Classical Visas tenant; browser automation renders remote content by definition, so a sandbox escape is live wherever a browser verb is invoked. What bounds it TODAY is usage, not architecture: all six verbs (web.fetch, browser.doctor, browser.tab.open, browser.remote.start, browser.remote.stop, browser.page.info) have ZERO rows in that tenant's audit_log - never once invoked - and the second tenant registers no browser adapter at all. Usage is a weak bound because it changes the day someone calls a verb, with no code or config change, which is why the expiry is six weeks rather than the usual year. Prefer deactivating browser-cli where unused, or dropping chromium from the image, over renewing this.
accepted.note: sandbox escape via crafted HTML. Trivy reports fixed 151.0.7922.47-1, which is the UPSTREAM CHROME version, not a Debian package. Measured 2026-07-31: bookworm and bookworm-security both offer exactly 150.0.7871.181-1~deb12u1, and trixie the same code as -1~deb13u1, so no Debian release carries the fix and no rebuild or base change takes it. Follows the ratio of [2026] VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001. Surfaced only because PR #198 was the first change today to go through a pull request rather than a direct push with branch protection bypassed.
accepted.reason: No Debian release carries the fix. Measured 2026-07-31: bookworm and bookworm-security both offer exactly the installed 150.0.7871.181-1~deb12u1, and trixie the same code as -1~deb13u1. Trivy's 'fixed 151.0.7922.47-1' is the upstream Chrome version, not a package, so no rebuild or base change takes it. Follows the ratio of [2026] VJS-CC-BOLTRIG-SUPPLY-CHAIN-ADVISORY-ACCEPTANCE-001: accept only where the fix cannot be taken, and only as a record.
accepted.compensating_control: Bounded by USAGE, not by architecture, and that is a weaker control than the other entries in this file carry - stated plainly rather than dressed up. What holds today: the fleet worker runs under x-app-hardening with a read_only root filesystem and only /tmp writable; chromium is launched only through the browser-cli adapter, which is registered on ONE tenant and has ZERO invocations of any of its six verbs (web.fetch, browser.doctor, browser.tab.open, browser.remote.start, browser.remote.stop, browser.page.info) in that tenant's audit_log; the second production tenant registers no browser adapter at all; and the adapter is HITL-gated at the dispatch chokepoint like every other outbound verb, so a browser call cannot run unattended. NONE of that prevents a sandbox escape once a browser verb IS invoked against hostile content - it only means nothing has invoked one yet. The durable fix is to deactivate browser-cli where it is unused, or drop chromium from the image, and this entry should be closed that way rather than renewed.
